articles.title: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen
articles.summary: Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’ • This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
body: Joshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.

Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised star Sacha Baron Cohen early in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.

The movie involves Loudermilk being recruited by another Cohen character, the ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, to help form a citizens’ warrior force to protect US borders, making use of his top-secret new weapon: a gun disguised as buttocks.

Along with fellow recruit Michael Aboud, the chair of the El Paso county Republican party, Loudermilk joins Morad on a mission to stop the birth on US soil of the baby of a fictional South American drugs kinpin. This involves abducting a woman apparently in labour, abandoning her in a deserted medical facility, kidnapping her newborn child (a lifelike prosthetic) and driving it in a zipped bag to the border in order to deliver it by drone to Mexico.

articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Director Lance Oppenheim Says Billy Evans ‘Didn’t Care About Being Seen Naked’; Evans Asked, ‘Want to Film Me Showering?’
articles.summary: “You Can See Everything” audiences were expecting to be taken aback for a variety of reasons when watching the documentary, but a full-frontal shot of Elizabeth Holmes’ partner Billy Evans wasn’t something many foresaw experiencing in the theater.
body: “So I don’t know what that means, but I feel like there’s enough stuff in there that gives me the impression that maybe he was excited that people could see everything and that there was full access, I guess,” Oppenheim continued. “But it really beats me, honestly. We were in the car ride on the way back from the gym, and I said to Billy, ‘We will give you some time to shower.’ And Billy responded, ‘Want to film me showering?’ I offered to film him in a way that could avoid seeing his genitals, but Billy said he didn’t care about being seen naked.”

Ahead of the film’s release earlier this month, Evans admitted he hadn’t seen the doc while appearing on the “All-In” podcast. “I haven’t seen it. I might think this is the dumbest thing I have ever done,” Evans said on the podcast, admitting that Holmes “looks insane” in the trailer.

Before hitting theaters on Oct. 16, “You Can See Everything” had been quietly in the works from Fielder and Oppenheim for more than three years. The doc offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors.

articles.title: Peggy King, ‘George Gobel Show’ Actress and Singer of the ’50s, Dies at 96
articles.summary: Peggy King, a 1950s television and recording star, died Sunday following a battle with Alzheimer’s at the Saunders House Assisted Living facility in Wynnewood, Pa. She was 96. King’s publicist, Alan Eicher, confirmed her death. King was a regular on the “George Gobel Show” from 1954-57.
body: In 1952, she signed to an MGM contract, which led to a cameo in Vincente Minnelli’s “The Bad and the Beautiful,” in which she sang on the soundtrack album. She also appeared in “Abbott and Costello Meet the Mummy.”

Mitch Miller signed her to a long-term contract with Columbia Records, where she made two best-selling albums. She had a string of hit singles, and composer Arthur Hamilton wrote “Cry Me a River” for her but Miller would not let her record the song.

King starred with Tab Hunter in the television musical “Hans Brinker or the Silver Skates.” She also starred in a TV musical version of “Jack and the Beanstalk” with Joel Grey, Celeste Holm and Cyril Ritchard. She played a stewardess in the 1957 thriller “Zero Hour!” with Dana Andrews and Linda Danell.

She was inducted into the Broadcast Pioneers Hall of Fame in 2010 and was among the first celebrities honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. King’s last released recording was the album “Songs a la King,” released in 2016. She performed regularly in the Philadelphia area, New York and Los Angeles as late as 2014.

articles.summary: Hudson Williams is working on a new film and is “getting tripped up” over a “Heated Rivalry” parallel. Prior to the success of the Canadian queer hockey romance that catapulted the actor to fame over the past year, Williams wrote and directed several short films, including “Soakers,” “Buttons” and…
body: “I’m writing a movie right now, but one character is an ex-hockey player,” he said. “We were like, ‘But if we have this hockey player and then you’ve done a hockey show…’ We’re getting tripped up on it and we’re considering other sports, but for some reason this character just made way more sense being an ex-hockey player. It’s almost like you have to bust through the prison of your own mind or construct of your own mind.”

The actor did not elaborate on the nature of the project. It’s far from the only thing Williams is currently or recently working on: “Yaga” premiered on Oct. 23, and production began on the second season of “Heated Rivalry” in August. He will also appear in the dark comedic thriller “Apparatus” opposite Dylan O’Brien, and in the ensemble culinary thriller “Tyrant” with Charlize Theron, Julia Garner, Demi Moore and Omar Apollo.

articles.title: ‘Wicker’ Stars Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård and Elizabeth Debicki on Making the ‘Very Silly,’ ‘Really Heartbreaking’ Film: ‘It’s Not Just a Slapstick or Sex Comedy’
articles.summary: When Elizabeth Debicki arrived on set for “Wicker,” the first thing she saw was Alexander Skarsgård wading through water — full-frontal. But it wasn’t Skarsgård in the flesh; he was “stark naked as wicker.” “I turned the corner, and I was like, ‘Hi, Alex!’ and I went bright red because my brain…
body: While Debicki needed a moment to grapple with the sight of a naked wicker man, Colman’s reaction mirrored her character falling in love at first sight.
“It was amazing because we’d all been looking at images for 18 months or so, and then to see it in the flesh, it was amazing,” Colman said. “That [feeling] of, ‘Oh my god, it’s going to work!’

The Oscar winner was the first to see Skarsgård in his full wicker suit and prosthetic makeup. The prototype had been sculpted after Skarsgård’s features, but when the Weta Workshop artists tried it on someone else in New Zealand, it almost worked, but not quite.

“If it doesn’t quite work, it looks like a horror film because it looks like you cut someone’s face off and glued it onto your own, and that wasn’t quite the tone we wanted to go for here,” Skarsgård explains. “So, it was a lot of anticipation and excitement and a lot of nerves because it was like, ‘Oh shit! If it doesn’t work, then we’re kind of screwed.”

articles.title: A Peek Into ‘SNL UK’: Strict Security, Giddy Cynthia Erivo and Sometimes More a Party Than a TV Set
articles.summary: With Amelia Dimoldenberg and Ike Barinholtz among the audience members at Saturday's lively — and impressively huge — season two finale, we wonder: Has the British spin-off finally found its groove?
body: The Hollywood Reporter was gifted one of London’s hottest tickets on Saturday night: a seat at the season two finale of SNL UK.

The Sky spinoff of Lorne Michaels’ long-running NBC sketch show boasted solid viewership numbers in its first installment earlier this year, led by SNL hall-of-famer Tina Fey. Her inaugural episode notched up over 220,000 viewers in Britain, and despite the sharp drop toward the end of the season — Ncuti Gatwa’s closer, up against the Eurovision Song Contest, ended on a series low of 86,420 — critic response was generally fairly warm.

With two seasons officially under its belt, SNL UK naysayers continue to ask: Can this very American format make Brits laugh? The answer is yes. This cast, steadfast in its commitment to appealing to a very British sensibility, sticks to jokes that probably have Barinholtz and Caplan a little stumped. Think Noel Fielding’s odd posture on The Great British Bake Off, a Walthamstow wedding crashed by a rapper who can’t bury her beef with Thames Water, and a princess trapped in a tower throwing a can of Lilt at her rescuer: The target audience here is deliberately specific.
points: With Amelia Dimoldenberg and Ike Barinholtz among the audience members at Saturday's lively — and impressively huge — season two finale, we wonder: Has the British spin-off finally found its groove?

articles.title: ‘Young Sheldon’ Star Emily Osment Requested Intimacy Coordinator Over Age Gap With Montana Jordan: “He Was a Baby!”
articles.summary: The actress, who was 30 when she joined the CBS series, recalled feeling "uncomfortable" about the age difference between her and her 18-year-old onscreen love interest.
body: Young Sheldon star Emily Osment recalls requesting an intimacy coordinator during her time on the CBS series because of the age gap between her and co-star Montana Jordan. Osment, who played Mandy McAllister, was 30 when she joined the series in 2022, while Jordan, who played George Cooper, was 18.

“That made me uncomfortable. He was a baby! A baby with a mullet,” Osment said. “So I spoke to Tim Marx, and obviously they were not able to get one that late in the day, but for the next few episodes they had one there, since the relationship between them escalates. It made everything easier having one there. I think it’s something that’s really important.”

“I don’t know if Montana even knew if he could ask for that. Like, let’s give him the option, too. Make him comfortable. And he’s such a sweet kid, I think he would just eat his discomfort,” she continued. “But I love those guys, and I’m really happy it got to the point where they were able to do that [for us].”

Elsewhere in the book, director Alex Reid acknowledged that production initially “dropped the ball” and overlooked having an intimacy coordinator, saying that the team’s decision was influenced by the show’s lack of sex scenes.

articles.title: Danny Boyle's Trippy 2013 Thriller Features James McAvoy's Most Underrated Performance
articles.summary: James McAvoy, Rosario Dawson, and more light up the screen in this 2013 Danny Boyle thriller, which finds the director scratching his Brian De Palma itch.
body: Danny Boyle was on a scorchingly hot streak heading into 2013's "Trance." His "Slumdog Millionaire" took home eight Academy Awards in 2009, including Best Picture and Best Director, and he followed that up with the terrifically intense survival drama "127 Hours" (which didn't win any Oscars but was nominated for six). So, he rolled that momentum into "Trance," which was touted as a back-to-basics thriller starring James McAvoy, Rosario Dawson, and Vincent Cassel. And he was going to need this palate cleaner, too, because he'd just landed the assignment of a lifetime: directing the Opening Ceremony of the 2012 Summer Olympics in London.

Critics were mixed as to whether he pulled it all together, but I think "Trance" is a superlative piece of pure cinema that finds Boyle scratching his Brian De Palma and Nicolas Roeg itch. It's weird, a little surreal, and sexy as hell, with McAvoy doing some of his most underrated work.

articles.title: A Twilight Zone Episode Based On A Real-Life Experience Inspired Jordan Peele's Us
articles.summary: Jordan Peele's Us was inspired by a Twilight Zone episode involving doppelgängers, itself based on a creepy real-life encounter that Rod Serling had.
body: "Mirror Image" is the 21st episode of "The Twilight Zone" Season 1. It features "Psycho" star Vera Miles as Millicent Barnes, a woman who, while waiting at a bus station, is distressed to be told by both the ticket agent and the bathroom attendant that she has already spoken to them despite having no memory of having done so. Soon, she realizes that a sinister "twin" has somehow arrived to try to replace her. Nobody at the bus station believes her, however, and like so many others who unwittingly entered the Twilight Zone before and after her, Millicent begins to question her own sanity.

As does Martin Milner's Paul Grinstead, a kindly man who initially seems drawn to Millicent but becomes concerned when she starts talking about how her doppelgänger has somehow crossed the divide between parallel worlds and is out to get her. "In order to survive, it has to take over," she tells Paul. "Replace Us. Move us out so that it can live." After Paul has Millicent taken away by police, he very quickly learns that she may have been of sound mind after all, as his own "twin" is now lurking in the same bus station.
points: Jordan Peele's Us was inspired by a Twilight Zone episode involving doppelgängers, itself based on a creepy real-life encounter that Rod Serling had.

articles.title: Peggy King, Singer and ‘George Gobel Show’ Star of Television’s Golden Age, Dies at 96
articles.summary: She also recorded several albums for Columbia Records and appeared in Vincente Minnelli’s 'The Bad and the Beautiful.'
body: Peggy King, a television star and singer who rose to prominence in the 1950s, has died. She was 96.
King died Sunday after a long battle with Alzheimer’s disease, her publicist Alan Eicher announced. She had been residing at the Saunders House assisted living facility in Wynnewood, Pennsylvania.

Throughout the 1950s, King appeared on numerous variety programs, including The Bob Hope Show, American Bandstand, The Steve Allen Show, The Jack Benny Program and The Perry Como Show. She also guest-starred on classic television series including Maverick and Dragnet.

King signed a contract with MGM in 1952, leading to a singing cameo in Vincente Minnelli’s film The Bad and the Beautiful, in which she performed “Don’t Blame Me.” She later appeared in the 1955 horror-comedy Abbott and Costello Meet the Mummy.

articles.title: George Clooney Helped Make An HBO Series That Was Canceled After One Season
articles.summary: One of George Clooney's many projects included producing this HBO comedy series that didn't last more than one season (and isn't even streaming on HBO now).
body: George Clooney is a revered Hollywood figure with an esteemed career and good reputation. The best George Clooney movies are some of the best movies of the last several decades, and outside of that one time he played Batman, the man can seemingly do no wrong. But Clooney actually has a few questionable entries on his filmography. "Unscripted," the 2005 comedy drama series he produced and helped direct, is one example.

True to its name, "Unscripted" was mostly improvised by its cast, which included Bryan Greenberg, Krista Allen, and Jennifer Hall playing fictionalized versions of themselves. The trio improvised their way through scenes that depicted them as struggling actors looking for their big break under the guidance of their acting teacher, Goddard Fulton (Frank Langella). Langella wasn't the only Clooney affiliate involved with the show either, as several of the star's A-list friends showed up throughout the first and only season. Sadly, that wasn't enough to save "Unscripted" from being canceled after its ten-episode run.
